units.name: Unit 1: Introduction to SE & Requirements Engineering

topics.name: What is Software Engineering
topics.description: A disciplined, systematic approach to designing, building, and maintaining software, as opposed to writing code ad hoc.

topics.name: SDLC
topics.description: Software Development Life Cycle — the standard stages a project passes through: requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, maintenance.

topics.name: Agile methodology
topics.description: An iterative development approach that delivers working software in short cycles and adapts to changing requirements, instead of planning everything upfront.

topics.name: Scrum
topics.description: A specific Agile framework organized around fixed-length sprints, daily stand-ups, and defined roles like Scrum Master and Product Owner.

topics.name: Requirements elicitation
topics.description: The process of gathering what stakeholders actually need from the system, through interviews, surveys, or observation.

topics.name: Functional requirements
topics.description: Statements of what the system must do — specific features and behaviors.

topics.name: Non-functional requirements
topics.description: Requirements about how the system performs its functions — e.g. speed, security, reliability — rather than what it does.

topics.name: Software Requirement Specification (SRS)
topics.description: A formal document that fully describes a system's intended functionality, used as the reference for design and testing.

topics.name: Requirement Traceability Matrix
topics.description: A table linking each requirement to the design, code, and test cases that implement and verify it.

topics.name: UML use case diagrams
topics.description: Diagrams showing how different users (actors) interact with a system's features (use cases).

topics.name: Test planning
topics.description: Deciding in advance what will be tested, how, and by whom, before development begins.

topics.name: Project management (PM) role
topics.description: Coordinating people, schedules, and resources so a software project is delivered on time and within scope.

topics.name: Time estimation & scheduling
topics.description: Predicting how long tasks will take and sequencing them so the project has a realistic timeline.

topics.name: Risk management
topics.description: Identifying things that could go wrong in a project and planning how to prevent or respond to them.

topics.name: Gantt chart
topics.description: A bar-chart timeline showing project tasks against time, used to track schedule and dependencies.

topics.name: Software architecture
topics.description: The high-level structure of a system — its major components and how they interact — decided before detailed design.

topics.name: Design patterns
topics.description: Reusable, proven solutions to common software design problems.

topics.name: Microservices
topics.description: An architecture style where an application is built as many small, independently deployable services rather than one large program.

topics.name: Modularity (API & ABI)
topics.description: Breaking a system into independent, interchangeable parts; an API defines how modules talk to each other in code, an ABI defines it at the binary level.

topics.name: Technical debt
topics.description: The extra future work created when a quick, imperfect solution is chosen now instead of a better one.

topics.name: Test-driven development (TDD)
topics.description: Writing a test for a feature before writing the code that implements it.

topics.name: AI for software engineering
topics.description: Using AI tools to assist with writing, reviewing, or reasoning about code during development.

topics.name: Coding standards & guidelines
topics.description: Agreed-upon rules for how code should be written, to keep a codebase consistent and readable across a team.

topics.name: Code review
topics.description: Having another developer examine your code changes before they're merged, to catch bugs and improve quality.

topics.name: CI/CD pipeline
topics.description: Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment — automated processes that build, test, and release code changes frequently and reliably.

topics.name: DevSecOps
topics.description: Integrating security practices directly into the development and operations pipeline, rather than checking for security only at the end.

topics.name: Static and dynamic testing
topics.description: Static testing examines code without running it (e.g. code review); dynamic testing runs the program to observe its actual behavior.

topics.name: Software Configuration Management (SCM)
topics.description: Tracking and controlling changes to a project's code and files over time, typically via version control.

topics.name: Defect and bug management
topics.description: The process of logging, prioritizing, fixing, and verifying fixes for issues found in software.

topics.name: Patch and release management
topics.description: Planning how updates and fixes are packaged and delivered to users in a controlled way.

topics.name: Quality metrics & measurements
topics.description: Quantifiable indicators (e.g. defect density, test coverage) used to judge how good a piece of software is.

topics.name: Risk management for quality
topics.description: Identifying what could cause quality failures and planning to reduce that risk before it happens.

topics.name: Code coverage
topics.description: A measurement of what percentage of the code was actually executed while running the test suite.

topics.name: Ethics in AI usage
topics.description: Considering the responsible, fair, and transparent use of AI tools and AI-generated code in software projects.

topics.name: Software patents
topics.description: Legal protection that can be granted for a novel software invention, giving the owner exclusive rights to it.

topics.name: System testing
topics.description: Testing the complete, integrated system as a whole, rather than individual components.

topics.name: Security validation & penetration testing
topics.description: Deliberately probing a system for security weaknesses the way an attacker would, to find and fix them first.

topics.name: Fuzzing
topics.description: A testing technique that feeds a program random or malformed input to try to trigger crashes or unexpected behavior.

topics.name: Software evolution & maintenance
topics.description: The ongoing process of updating and fixing software after it's released, as needs and environments change.

units.name: Unit 1: Foundations of HCI & UX Design

topics.name: What is HCI
topics.description: The study of how people interact with computers and digital systems, and how to design that interaction well.

topics.name: Human factors: Perception
topics.description: How people notice and interpret visual, auditory, and tactile information from an interface.

topics.name: Human factors: Cognition
topics.description: How people think, reason, and make decisions while using an interface.

topics.name: Human factors: Memory
topics.description: How much information users can hold in mind while completing a task, and how interfaces should avoid overloading it.

topics.name: Mental models
topics.description: The user's internal understanding of how a system works, which may or may not match how it actually works.

topics.name: Norman's interaction model
topics.description: Don Norman's framework describing the gap between what a user intends to do (Gulf of Execution) and how they interpret the result (Gulf of Evaluation).

topics.name: User-Centered Design (UCD)
topics.description: A design process that repeatedly involves real users at every stage, rather than designing based on assumptions alone.

topics.name: UX research: Interviews
topics.description: One-on-one conversations with users to understand their needs, habits, and pain points.

topics.name: UX research: Surveys
topics.description: Structured questionnaires used to gather user feedback at scale.

topics.name: UX research: Observation
topics.description: Watching users interact with a product in a real or simulated setting to see actual behavior, not just stated opinions.

topics.name: Affinity diagramming
topics.description: A technique for grouping related research findings or ideas into clusters to spot patterns.

topics.name: Personas
topics.description: Fictional profiles representing typical user types, used to keep design decisions grounded in real user needs.

topics.name: Empathy mapping
topics.description: A tool that maps what a user says, thinks, feels, and does, to build a fuller picture of their experience.

topics.name: User journey mapping
topics.description: A visual timeline of the steps a user takes to complete a goal, including their emotions at each step.

topics.name: Information architecture
topics.description: The way content and navigation are structured so users can find what they need.

topics.name: Design principles: Affordances
topics.description: Visual cues that suggest how an object or element should be used (e.g. a button that looks pressable).

topics.name: Design principles: Feedback
topics.description: Signals the system gives to confirm that a user's action had an effect.

topics.name: Design principles: Consistency
topics.description: Using the same patterns and behavior throughout an interface so users don't have to relearn things.

topics.name: Interaction styles
topics.description: The different ways users can interact with a system — e.g. typing commands, tapping a GUI, speaking, or gesturing.

topics.name: Design thinking
topics.description: A problem-solving approach that cycles through empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing.

topics.name: Typography
topics.description: The choice and arrangement of fonts to make text readable and set visual tone.

topics.name: Color theory
topics.description: Principles for choosing and combining colors to create contrast, hierarchy, and mood.

topics.name: Layout & spacing
topics.description: How elements are arranged and separated on a screen to guide the eye and avoid clutter.

topics.name: Visual hierarchy
topics.description: Arranging elements so the most important ones draw attention first.

topics.name: Wireframing
topics.description: A simplified, low-detail sketch of a screen's layout, used early to plan structure before visual design.

topics.name: Low-fidelity prototypes
topics.description: Rough, quick mockups (often just sketches) used to test ideas cheaply before investing in detail.

topics.name: High-fidelity prototypes
topics.description: Polished, realistic mockups that closely resemble the final product, used for detailed testing.

topics.name: Interface design guidelines
topics.description: Official design standards (e.g. Google Material Design, Apple Human Interface Guidelines) that define consistent platform behavior.

topics.name: Responsive design
topics.description: Designing interfaces that adapt cleanly to different screen sizes and devices.

topics.name: Usability: Learnability
topics.description: How easily a new user can figure out how to use the system.

topics.name: Usability: Efficiency
topics.description: How quickly an experienced user can complete tasks.

topics.name: Usability: Memorability
topics.description: How easily a returning user can remember how to use the system after time away.

topics.name: Usability: Error prevention
topics.description: Designing to stop users from making mistakes, or making mistakes easy to recover from.

topics.name: Heuristic evaluation
topics.description: Experts review an interface against a known set of usability principles to spot problems.

topics.name: Cognitive walkthrough
topics.description: Evaluators step through a task as a new user would, checking whether each step is understandable.

topics.name: User testing
topics.description: Watching real users attempt tasks with the product to find usability issues directly.

topics.name: Think-aloud protocol
topics.description: A testing method where users verbalize their thoughts while using the product, revealing confusion in real time.

topics.name: A/B testing
topics.description: Comparing two versions of a design with real users to see which performs better.

topics.name: SUS (System Usability Scale)
topics.description: A standard 10-question survey used to score a product's perceived usability.

topics.name: WCAG
topics.description: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines — the standard rules for making digital content usable by people with disabilities.

topics.name: Dark patterns
topics.description: Manipulative design choices that trick users into actions they didn't intend (e.g. hidden unsubscribe buttons).

units.name: Unit 4: Emerging Trends in UI/UX & HCI

topics.name: AI in HCI
topics.description: Using AI (chatbots, recommenders, personalization) to shape or adapt the user experience.

topics.name: Conversational UI
topics.description: Interfaces where users interact through natural language, like chatbots or voice assistants.

topics.name: Voice User Interfaces (VUI)
topics.description: Interfaces controlled entirely by spoken commands, with no visual screen required.

topics.name: VR/AR interfaces
topics.description: Interfaces for virtual reality (fully simulated) or augmented reality (digital overlays on the real world).

topics.name: Brain-computer interfaces
topics.description: Systems that let users control a device directly through brain signals, without physical input.

topics.name: Cross-cultural UI/UX
topics.description: Designing interfaces that work appropriately across different languages, cultures, and reading directions.

topics.name: Ethical & social implications of HCI
topics.description: Considering how interface design choices affect user wellbeing, privacy, and society at large.

topics.name: Persuasive design
topics.description: Design intentionally used to influence user behavior — can be ethical (habit-building) or exploitative (dark patterns).

topics.name: Android development environment
topics.description: The toolchain (Android Studio, SDKs, emulators) used to build and test Android apps.

topics.name: Kotlin variables & nullable types
topics.description: Kotlin distinguishes types that can hold null (nullable, marked with ?) from types that can never be null, catching null-related bugs at compile time.

topics.name: Conditional statements & loops
topics.description: Control-flow constructs (if/when, for, while) that let a program branch or repeat based on conditions.

topics.name: Functions & lambdas
topics.description: Reusable blocks of code; lambdas are small, unnamed functions that can be passed around as values.

topics.name: Collections
topics.description: Built-in structures (lists, sets, maps) for storing and operating on groups of values.

topics.name: Classes & objects
topics.description: Blueprints (classes) for creating structured data with behavior, and the actual instances (objects) created from them.

topics.name: Inheritance
topics.description: A mechanism where one class can reuse and extend the behavior of another class.

topics.name: Data classes
topics.description: A concise Kotlin class type designed specifically to hold data, with equality and printing behavior generated automatically.

topics.name: Exception handling
topics.description: Code structures (try/catch) that let a program detect and recover from runtime errors instead of crashing.

units.name: Unit 2: UI Development with Jetpack Compose

topics.name: Android app fundamentals
topics.description: The core building blocks of an Android app — Activities (screens), Services (background work), and BroadcastReceivers (system events).

topics.name: Jetpack Compose
topics.description: Android's modern toolkit for building UI declaratively in Kotlin code, instead of separate XML layout files.

topics.name: Composables
topics.description: Functions marked to describe a piece of UI, which Compose can render and re-render automatically.

topics.name: State management
topics.description: Tracking values that can change over time (like text input) so the UI automatically updates when they do.

topics.name: LazyColumn / LazyRow
topics.description: Compose components that efficiently display long scrolling lists by only rendering the items currently visible.

topics.name: Scaffold
topics.description: A Compose layout structure that provides standard screen elements like a top bar, bottom bar, and content area.

topics.name: Compose navigation
topics.description: The system for moving between different screens (composables) within an app.

topics.name: Intents
topics.description: Objects used to request an action from another app component, like starting a new screen or sharing data.

topics.name: BroadcastReceivers
topics.description: Components that listen for and respond to system-wide or app-wide broadcast events.

topics.name: Services
topics.description: Components that run tasks in the background, without a user interface, even if the user isn't actively using the app.

topics.name: SharedPreferences
topics.description: A simple key-value storage system for saving small amounts of app data, like settings.

topics.name: Room database
topics.description: An Android library that provides a structured way to store and query local data using SQLite under the hood.

topics.name: Resources
topics.description: Non-code assets (strings, images, layouts) that are kept separate from source code so they can be managed and localized easily.

topics.name: Retrofit
topics.description: A popular Android library for making HTTP network requests to web APIs in a type-safe way.

topics.name: Glide
topics.description: A library for efficiently loading and caching images from the internet into an app's UI.

topics.name: Application signing
topics.description: Digitally signing an app package to verify its authenticity before it can be published or installed.

topics.name: Play Store deployment
topics.description: The process of packaging and publishing an Android app so it becomes available to users on Google Play.

topics.name: Device sensors & camera
topics.description: Hardware features (accelerometer, GPS, camera, etc.) that apps can access through Android APIs.

topics.name: Firebase integration
topics.description: Using Google's Firebase platform for backend features like authentication, databases, or push notifications.

topics.name: ML Kit / GenAI APIs
topics.description: Google's on-device machine learning and generative AI APIs that apps can call to add smart features.

topics.name: Purpose & view of data
topics.description: Why databases exist — to store, organize, and retrieve data reliably, presenting different views to different users.

topics.name: Database application architecture
topics.description: How an application's layers (client, application logic, database) are structured and communicate.

topics.name: E-R Model
topics.description: Entity-Relationship Model — a way of designing a database by identifying entities (things), their attributes, and the relationships between them.

topics.name: Reducing ER to relational schema
topics.description: The process of converting an E-R diagram into actual database tables and columns.

topics.name: Relational algebra
topics.description: A formal set of operations (select, project, join, etc.) used to query and manipulate relational data mathematically.

topics.name: SQL overview
topics.description: Structured Query Language — the standard language for defining, querying, and manipulating relational databases.

topics.name: Data definition (DDL)
topics.description: SQL commands used to define database structure, such as CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE.

topics.name: Constraints & keys
topics.description: Rules (primary key, foreign key, unique, not null) that enforce data integrity in a table.

units.name: Unit 2: Advanced SQL in Database Design

topics.name: Database modification (DML)
topics.description: SQL commands that change data — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.

topics.name: Set operations
topics.description: SQL operations (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) that combine or compare the results of multiple queries.

topics.name: Aggregate functions & grouping
topics.description: Functions like COUNT, SUM, AVG that compute a single value across a group of rows, often combined with GROUP BY.

topics.name: Nested & correlated subqueries
topics.description: A query written inside another query; correlated subqueries reference values from the outer query, re-running per row.

topics.name: Join expressions
topics.description: SQL operations that combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column.

topics.name: Views
topics.description: A saved, named SQL query that behaves like a virtual table when queried.

topics.name: Triggers
topics.description: Database code that runs automatically in response to a specific event, like a row being inserted or updated.

topics.name: Stored procedures & functions
topics.description: Reusable blocks of SQL logic saved in the database itself, callable like a function.

topics.name: Common Table Expressions (CTE)
topics.description: A temporary, named result set defined within a query using WITH, used to simplify complex SQL.

topics.name: Window functions
topics.description: Functions that perform calculations across a set of rows related to the current row, without collapsing them into one result like GROUP BY does.

topics.name: Query processing & optimization
topics.description: How a database decides the most efficient way to execute a given SQL query.

topics.name: Functional dependencies
topics.description: A relationship where one attribute's value determines another attribute's value in a table, used as the basis for normalization.

topics.name: Normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF)
topics.description: A series of rules for organizing tables to reduce data redundancy and avoid update anomalies.

topics.name: Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
topics.description: A stricter version of 3NF that removes remaining anomalies caused by certain functional dependencies.

topics.name: Database transactions
topics.description: A sequence of operations treated as a single unit — either all of them succeed, or none do.

topics.name: Concurrency control
topics.description: Techniques that let multiple transactions run at the same time without corrupting each other's data.

topics.name: Locking
topics.description: A concurrency control mechanism that restricts access to data while a transaction is using it, to prevent conflicts.

topics.name: NoSQL databases
topics.description: Databases that don't use the traditional relational table model, often designed for flexibility or scale (e.g. document, key-value stores).

topics.name: Key-value databases
topics.description: A simple NoSQL model that stores data as pairs of a unique key and its associated value.

topics.name: Graph databases
topics.description: Databases optimized for storing and querying data as nodes and relationships, useful for highly connected data.

topics.name: Vector databases
topics.description: Databases designed to store and search high-dimensional vectors, commonly used for AI similarity search.

units.name: Unit 1: Introduction, Metrics, Decision Trees & KNN

topics.name: What is Machine Learning
topics.description: A field of AI where systems learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed with rules.

topics.name: Concept learning & hypothesis space
topics.description: Learning a general rule (hypothesis) from labeled examples that correctly classifies new, unseen data.

topics.name: Performance metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall
topics.description: Accuracy is overall correctness; precision is how many predicted positives were actually correct; recall is how many actual positives were correctly found.

topics.name: ROC & AUC
topics.description: ROC is a curve plotting a classifier's true-positive vs false-positive rate at different thresholds; AUC summarizes it as a single score.

topics.name: Bias-variance tradeoff
topics.description: The balance between a model being too simple to capture patterns (high bias) and too sensitive to noise in training data (high variance).

topics.name: Cross validation
topics.description: A technique for testing a model's performance by training and evaluating it on different splits of the data, to get a reliable estimate.

topics.name: Decision Trees
topics.description: A model that makes predictions by following a series of if-then splits on feature values, shaped like a tree.

topics.name: Overfitting
topics.description: When a model learns the training data too closely, including its noise, and performs poorly on new data.

topics.name: Logistic Regression
topics.description: A classification algorithm that predicts the probability of a binary outcome using a linear combination of inputs.

topics.name: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
topics.description: A classification method that predicts a data point's label based on the labels of its closest neighbors in the training data.

topics.name: Artificial Neural Networks (ANN)
topics.description: Models loosely inspired by the brain, made of layers of connected nodes that learn to map inputs to outputs.

topics.name: Perceptron
topics.description: The simplest type of neural network unit, which makes a binary decision based on a weighted sum of its inputs.

topics.name: Multi-layer networks & backpropagation
topics.description: Networks with hidden layers between input and output, trained by backpropagation — an algorithm that adjusts weights based on prediction error.

topics.name: Activation functions
topics.description: Functions (e.g. Sigmoid, ReLU, Tanh) applied at each neuron that let a network learn non-linear patterns.

topics.name: Optimizers (SGD, Adam, etc.)
topics.description: Algorithms that adjust a model's weights during training to minimize prediction error efficiently.

topics.name: Support Vector Machines (SVM)
topics.description: A classification algorithm that finds the best boundary (hyperplane) separating classes by maximizing the margin between them.

topics.name: Kernel functions
topics.description: Functions that let SVMs separate data that isn't linearly separable, by implicitly mapping it into a higher-dimensional space.

topics.name: Boosting
topics.description: An ensemble technique that combines many weak models sequentially, each correcting the errors of the previous one.

topics.name: Random Forest
topics.description: An ensemble method that builds many decision trees on random subsets of data and averages their predictions.

topics.name: Bayes' theorem
topics.description: A formula for updating the probability of a hypothesis as new evidence becomes available.

topics.name: Naive Bayes Classifier
topics.description: A simple probabilistic classifier that applies Bayes' theorem, assuming features are independent of each other.

topics.name: Maximum likelihood estimation
topics.description: A method for choosing model parameters that make the observed data most probable.

topics.name: Hidden Markov Models (HMM)
topics.description: A model for sequential data where the system is assumed to move through hidden (unobserved) states over time.

topics.name: Clustering
topics.description: Grouping data points into clusters based on similarity, without using labeled examples.

topics.name: K-Means clustering
topics.description: A clustering algorithm that partitions data into K groups by repeatedly assigning points to the nearest cluster center and updating centers.

topics.name: Reinforcement Learning basics
topics.description: A learning approach where an agent learns to make decisions by taking actions in an environment and receiving rewards or penalties.

topics.name: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)
topics.description: A neural network architecture specialized for processing grid-like data such as images, using convolution operations to detect patterns.

topics.name: Hyperparameter tuning
topics.description: The process of choosing the best configuration settings for a model (like learning rate) that aren't learned from data directly.

topics.name: MLOps
topics.description: Practices for reliably deploying, monitoring, and maintaining machine learning models in production, similar to DevOps for ML.
